# Flutter / Dart

- Write diagnostics through `NotificationLog`, never bare `Log`: `Log` throws when the host bound no `log` service, and every diagnostic sits in a `catch` or on a degradation path, where a second throw reaches the host as an unhandled error. `NotificationLog` asks `Magic.bound('log')` instead of wrapping the call in `try`/`catch`, so real logging failures still propagate.
- Read-state changes are optimistic: update `_notifications` and the stream first, then sync. On a throw `markAsRead` and `markAllAsRead` revert with `fetchNotifications()` and swallow the error, while `deleteNotification` re-adds the removed rows and rethrows, so a caller can tell a failed delete (screen and server disagree about something destructive) from a successful one. Keep that asymmetry.
- The package declares no push identity. `NotificationServiceProvider.boot` loads the persisted intent before it resolves a driver (the SDK replays a cold-start tap during `initialize`), then calls `reconcilePushIdentity()` once even with no driver, because a signed-out cold boot fires no auth event. `PushStateReporter` is the only code in `lib/` that listens to `Auth.stateNotifier` or `AuthLogout`.
- `notifications.push_state.external_id_prefix` (default `user_`) has to equal the prefix the app passes to `Notify.initializePush` and the backend addresses the device by: `PushStateReporter` reports a pass only for the intent `<prefix><Auth.id()>`, and OneSignal accepts a mismatched id and delivers to nobody. For `magic_starter` apps the same value lives in `magic_starter.notifications.external_id_prefix` and the backend's `MAGIC_STARTER_EXTERNAL_ID_PREFIX`; change all sides together.
